description: Chinese Infinite Flow fiction with stable overarching system mechanics and genre-appropriate terminology across changing scenario worlds.

style: Natural, polished English webnovel prose that preserves tension, horror, urgency, comedy, tactics, action, and character voice.
Preserve deliberate ambiguity and technically important explanations without adding explanations absent from the source.
Preserve each embedded world's genre and vocabulary instead of forcing every scenario into one stylistic register.
terminology_preservation_rules: Use established glossary renderings according to their status, with special consistency for formal system labels, missions, objectives, rewards, currencies, attributes, stats, bloodlines, enhancements, abilities, skills, ranks, and difficulty levels.

Keep overarching Infinite Flow system terminology stable across transitions while preserving the distinct supernatural, technological, military, historical, wuxia, cultivation, fantasy, game, or other terminology of the current embedded world.
Distinguish formal mechanically significant labels from the same Chinese words used as ordinary vocabulary.

Keep named worlds, scenarios, organizations, teams, abilities, bloodlines, enhancements, equipment, creatures, species, monsters, and recurring mechanics stable when context establishes them as terminology.
Preserve clearly identifiable established franchise proper names only when the source reference is unambiguous; do not invent franchise terminology from uncertain evidence.
Do not admit ordinary verbs, body parts, clothing, generic weapons or monsters, ordinary locations, emotions, combat actions, or one-off descriptions merely because a related category is allowed.
translation_policy.pinyin_preference: Chinese personal names normally use consistent romanization or pinyin; translate meaningful titles, aliases, epithets, team names, and descriptive proper names when the source and established novel style support it.
translation_policy.semantic_translation_preference: Prefer clear semantic English for formal system mechanics and descriptive named terms when accurate, while preserving established proper names and the terminology conventions appropriate to each embedded world.

terminology_distinctions: Distinguish ordinary vocabulary from formal system labels, named mechanics, and mechanically significant recurring terms.
Keep overarching system terminology consistent across scenarios without importing one embedded world's vocabulary into another.
Keep worlds and scenario names distinct from generic references to a world, place, stage, or situation.
Keep missions, mission types, objectives, rewards, currencies, ranks, difficulty levels, rules, and penalties as separate mechanical concepts.
Keep bloodlines, enhancements, classes, professions, attributes, stats, skills, abilities, techniques, and cultivation concepts distinct unless the source explicitly equates them.
Keep named items, equipment, weapons, artifacts, consumables, and materials distinct from generic objects.
Preserve unambiguous established franchise proper names; treat uncertain references conservatively and leave resolution to novel-specific glossary review.

review_priorities: Character names, aliases, forms of address, organizations, and teams must remain stable.
Formal system terminology must remain distinct from identical words used as ordinary vocabulary.
Mission names, mission types, objectives, rewards, currencies, ranks, difficulty levels, unlock conditions, penalties, rules, and mechanics require stable renderings when formally defined.
World and scenario names must remain consistent across transitions and must not be confused with generic descriptions.
Bloodlines, enhancements, classes, professions, attributes, stats, skills, abilities, techniques, and cultivation concepts must retain source distinctions.
Named items, equipment, weapons, artifacts, consumables, and materials enter the glossary when mechanically or narratively significant, not merely because they occur.
Recurring named creatures, species, and monsters require stable renderings; generic creatures do not.
Embedded-world terminology must follow that world's horror, science-fiction, military, historical, wuxia, cultivation, fantasy, game, or other genre context.
Unambiguous established franchise proper names should be preserved; uncertain identification should remain conservative and be flagged for review.
Reject ordinary vocabulary, mundane objects, generic actions, emotions, locations, weapons, monsters, and one-off descriptions.

priorities: Formal system terminology versus generic vocabulary.
Mission names, mission types, objectives, rewards, rules, unlock conditions, and penalties.
Named items, equipment, weapons, artifacts, consumables, and materials.
Ranks, evaluation labels, and difficulty levels.
Terminology carried consistently across scenario transitions.
Accidental terminology contamination between embedded worlds or genre registers.
Residual Chinese or CJK text in reader-facing English.
Inconsistent capitalization of formal names without indiscriminately capitalizing ordinary phrases.
